title: Predictable Confabulations: Factual Recall by LLMs Scales with Model Size and Topic Frequency
abstract: While scaling laws govern aggregate large language model performance, no scaling law has linked factual recall to both model size and training-data composition. We evaluated 38 models on over 8,900 scholarly references evaluated by an automated reference verification system. Recall quality follows a sigmoid in the log-linear combination of model parameter count and topic representation in training data. These two variables alone explain 60% of the variance across 16 dense models from four families, rising to 74-94% within individual families. The form matches a superposition-inspired account in which recall is gated by a signal-to-noise ratio: signal strength scales with concept frequency and the noise floor with model capacity.

significance.justification: The paper establishes a quantitative scaling law for factual recall that directly informs builders' model selection decisions based on parameter count and training data composition.

novelty.justification: While scaling laws exist for general performance, this is the first to specifically link factual recall to the combination of model size and topic frequency in training data with a sigmoid relationship.

reproducibility.justification: The method is clearly described with 38 models and 8,900 references evaluated, but no mention of code or dataset release for direct reproduction.

clarity.justification: The abstract clearly states the contribution, methodology, and results with specific numbers (60-94% variance explained) and a coherent theoretical framing.

topical_fit.justification: Directly addresses core LLM capabilities (factual recall) with practical implications for builders choosing models based on scaling behavior and training data characteristics.
